decisions.question: D3 cites bus-api@v1's bus_activation_test.dart and flutter-binding@v1's binding of the executor suite. Move the citations silently, or move them and record that each sentence and every gate still holds under the current fixtures?

options.label: Move and add a dated Checked paragraph
options.consequence: The reader sees that the sentences hold of the v2 text and that every --guarantee list still selects cases (42 and 52), at the cost of one paragraph

options.label: Move silently
options.consequence: Shorter, but the record's rule asks that a citation whose meaning could have changed be checked, and nothing would show it was

decisions.chosen: Move and add a dated Checked paragraph
decisions.why: The record's citation rule (DEC-804's reading) restates or checks a sentence rather than moving a version silently. Both sentences hold under v2: bus-api@v2's bus_activation_test.dart still binds topology-dsl@v2's live suite under ADR-001 item 9, and flutter-binding@v2's executor binding still lives in its own fixture directory. Counting the fixtures confirmed every gate: the navigation suite holds 42 cases, the new G13 case needs no bus and is selected by .3's list, and the executor suite holds 26 cases registered twice.

decisions.question: Where does navResolver construct the stage objects whose method tear-offs its stages hold (D5)?

options.label: Once per navResolver call, outside the declaration body
options.consequence: Every plan of one call's topology holds == stage functions, so re-activating that value returns its handle; another call's topology conflicts; passes the new G13 case (T4) and re-activates as P5 shows

options.label: Inside the declaration body
options.consequence: Named stages, but new receivers on every evaluation, so the resolver conflicts with its own second activation under bus-api@v2 G23 (P5) and fails the new G13 case (T4)

options.label: Canonicalized per configuration in a static cache
options.consequence: Another call of one configuration re-activates to the active handle, which G13 rules out, so it fails the same case (T4); the cache also holds the app's functions for the isolate's life

options.label: Closures
options.consequence: Unnamed edges in every graph and unequal to their own next evaluation; fails the naming case and the new G13 case (T4)

decisions.chosen: Once per navResolver call, outside the declaration body
decisions.why: navigation-api@v1 G13's last sentence, written at S62, requires it, and the declaration body runs on every planOf call (topology-dsl@v2 Interface) while bus-api@v2 G23 compares tear-offs by receiver identity. The S62 experiment ran all four stand-ins on both runtimes; only the once-per-call one passes both suites. The evidence moves from navigation-stage-names/, whose stand-in built the objects inside the declaration, to navigation-api-v0151/ T4 and P5. D5 keeps its id and title stem and gains a dated Restated paragraph.
evidence: topology-dsl@v2 G18 and its Interface comment on topology(...)

decisions.question: D6: with bus-api@v2 G18 sending a subscriber's error to the zone it listened in, does the executor still add no error handling of its own, and how is D6 restated?

options.label: Keep no error handling; restate both paths as reaching the constructor's zone
options.consequence: A throwing perform and an error event on the confirmations now reach one zone, the one the executor was constructed in; the executor goes on with later intents (P6); no declaration added

options.label: Catch a perform's error and report a new ShellDiagnostic
options.consequence: Compatible under navigation-api@v1 Versioning, but a declaration and a contract amend for a path no conforming router reaches

decisions.chosen: Keep no error handling; restate both paths as reaching the constructor's zone
decisions.why: The decision's reasons are unchanged and stronger: under v1 the two paths could land in two zones (P6 on the v1 runtime: bus zone and executor zone); under v2 both land in the zone that constructed the executor (P6 on the v2 runtime). The evidence moves from navigation-stage-names/ S3, which showed the confirmation path alone, to navigation-api-v0151/ P6, which shows both. It stays node-local because no conforming router produces either event.

decisions.question: nidana.navigation.6 reports LateExecutorConstruction when bus.lifecycle is running, and bus-api@v2 G34 makes the bus running from the moment start() begins. State the consistency in Scope only, or also pin it with a test of an executor constructed during start()?

options.label: State it and add a test
options.consequence: About 15 more lines of tests (size 360 to 375, within the PE); the phase verifies that an executor constructed from a bootstrap subscription's callback during start() is reported and works

options.label: State it in Scope only
options.consequence: No size change, but no case of either suite constructs an executor during start(), so nothing would check the reading

decisions.chosen: State it and add a test
decisions.why: No fixture covers construction during start(), and the probe shows the test is writable on a bus-api@v2 runtime: constructed from a callback of step 2 and of step 3, the executor sees BusLifecycle.running, is reported as LateExecutorConstruction, and performs the next resolved intent.

decisions.question: Does this plan emit an amend on navigation-api@v1 G19 stating that an executor constructed from the work start() runs is reported as LateExecutorConstruction?

options.label: No amend
options.consequence: G19's 'after start()' reads through bus-api@v2 G34, which already counts what start()'s work makes as made after start(); no contract change, no fixture case owed

options.label: Amend G19
options.consequence: Explicit for consumers, but reopens a stable, final contract for a dev-mode diagnostic in an edge no consumer reaches, and owes a case or a not-executable line

decisions.why: The plan settles no new semantics: the check reads bus.lifecycle, and bus-api@v2 G34 defines when the bus is running and what start()'s work counts as. The pending section records the reasoning under the navigation-api confirm. The signal that would have changed it: a consumer plan (nidana.flutter or nidana.integration) constructing an executor from a callback during start().

experiments.question: On a bus-api@v2 runtime, can a NavigationExecutor be constructed from a bootstrap subscription's callback during start(), is it reported as LateExecutorConstruction, and does it then work?
experiments.finding: Yes, from a callback of step 2 (first value) and of step 3 (queue delivery): the callback sees BusLifecycle.running, the one diagnostic is LateExecutorConstruction(origin: executor:during-start), and a later resolved intent is performed and written (stack [p/home, p/detail:2], nav.current-route p/detail). Run on the stand-in packages of navigation-api-v0151/ through its package configuration, without editing that experiment.
